---

Kis Ne Batao Zehar Diya Moula Hassan Ko

Teeron Se Kis Ne Surkh Kiya Is Kay Kafan Ko

Dozakh Banay Ga Joda Tera Ab To Thikanaa

Lanat Karay Ga Hashar Talak Tujh Peh Zamana

Tu Ne Zehar Jo De Diya Imam e Zaman Ko

Kya Janti Nahin Ti Yeh Ahmad Ka Sukhan Hai

Mera Hai Lakht e Jigar Hassan Mera Badan Hai

Kyun Maara Pahla Teer Mohammad Kay Badan Ko

Qasim Ki Maa Se Bolay Sheh e Hassan e Mujtaba

Mere Jigar Kay Tukray Kahin Farwa De Chupha

Qasim Bula Nah Laye Kaheen Meri Behan Ko

Qasim Kay Sar Seh Baap Kah Saya Hai Uth Gaya

Farwa Ne Ro Ke Zainab O Kulsoom Se Kaha

Ummat Ne Kaar Diya Hai Weeraan Meray Sahair Ko

Saar Main Hain Khaak Daalay Huway Log Jo Fida

Zainab Karay Gi Hashar Main Un Ke Liye Dua

De Ne Hain Aaye Pursa Jo Khatoun e Azan Ko.

from pathlib import Path
p = Path('src/data/lyrics/kis-ne-batao-zehar-diya-moula-hassan-ko-nw-886b26ecc7f9.md')
_, front, body = p.read_text().split('---', 2)
roman = '\\n'.join(line.removeprefix('  ') for line in front.split('romanLyrics: |-\\n')[1].splitlines())
for edition, digits in [(roman, '12345'), (body, '۱۲۳۴۵')]:
    blocks = [block.splitlines() for block in edition.strip().split('\\n\\n')]
    assert [len(block) for block in blocks] == [2,4,4,4,4,4]
    assert ''.join(block[0] for block in blocks[1:]) == digits
assert '\\u200c' not in body
print('Both editions contain 17 verses: a two-verse opening and five three-verse stanzas.')
PY"

item.text:
Reconstructed all 17 verses in Urdu script and preserved the Roman wording in `romanLyrics`. Verified that both versions have a two-verse opening and five three-verse stanzas. Updated the title metadata, set the direction to right-to-left, and removed the `noUrdu` tag.

I read the ambiguous Roman forms “Joda” as جعدہ, “Sahair” as شہر, and “Khatoun e Azan” as خاتونِ عزا.
